shell_keywords.purpose: shell words before a command word that are not the command

shell_names.purpose: shells that run a -c STRING, a nested command line that needs its own check (drift X3)

wrapper_names.purpose: prefix wrappers Unwrap sees through to the command they run (drift X1: no gtimeout)

wrapper_value_flags.purpose: wrapper -> flags that take the next word as their value (long forms also as --opt=val)

wrapper_operand_commands.purpose: wrappers that take one positional operand before their command (a duration, a priority)

git_global_value_flags.purpose: git global options whose value is the next word when not spelled with =

git_alias_proof_verbs.purpose: git verbs no alias can shadow; any other alias's first word is its real verb

conventional_commit_types.purpose: the Conventional Commits types a subject may open with

git_sdk_read_only_verbs.purpose: git verbs the Copilot SDK read-only gate allows (drift X6: the agent list has 14)

git_sdk_banned_flags.purpose: flags, abbreviations too, the SDK gate refuses: a program, config or driver, or --no-index (X6)

git_sdk_leading_flags.purpose: verb -> flags that must open its args: later, a value option or -- swallows them

git_sdk_verb_flags.purpose: verb -> its only dash args: branch must list, and git status -v runs textconv

pure_readers.purpose: commands that read, filter or copy their input and never run it (not awk, mysql or sed without -n)

evaluators.purpose: commands that read text as code: a string, a file or stdin, besides shells and interpreters (X4)

run_arg_commands.purpose: commands that run an argument as a command line or script, besides shells (X8: no parallel)

inert_commands.purpose: commands that print or search their arguments: a git-looking string there is text (X7)

inert_harness_verbs.purpose: claude-code verbs whose arguments are search terms, facts or PR text, never run

runner_value_flags.purpose: xargs, parallel and watch options whose value is the next word

go_run_value_flags.purpose: go run options whose value is the next word

rtk_runner_subcommands.purpose: rtk subcommands that run the command after them; the others are the command

c_string_commands.purpose: commands that run the string after their -c flag through a shell

git_path_flags.purpose: git flags, abbreviations too, whose value is a file git reads

agent_launchers.purpose: agent launcher binaries a dispatch-variable tamper check follows into

shell_declarers.purpose: builtins that declare or export a variable (drift X9: the mktemp rule names three)

kube_value_flags.purpose: kubectl and oc flags that take a value: the next word, =value, or attached to a short flag

kube_prod_flags.purpose: kubectl and oc flags whose value names the target cluster or namespace

kube_namespace_kinds.purpose: resource kinds that name a namespace or an OpenShift project

reserved_make_targets.purpose: make targets that write or ship the harness tree (build runs install, fmt and audit)

install_make_targets.purpose: make targets that replace the live install, refused from a harness worktree too

git_push_value_flags.purpose: git push options whose value is the next word, neither the remote nor a refspec

pipe_filters.purpose: commands that only read stdin and print it: none runs, writes or forwards its input

data_commands.purpose: commands that only print, search, store or hand on their words as text; none runs them

data_harness_verbs.purpose: claude-code verbs whose words are briefs, search terms, facts or PR text

branch_quiet_flags.purpose: git checkout and switch flags that neither discard nor overwrite

sudo_prefix_extras.purpose: runners the sudo guard sees through besides wrapper_names and shell_keywords (X1: no gtimeout)

agents_brief_verbs.purpose: claude-code agents verbs whose words are a brief, never run here

runner_names.purpose: commands that take their input or arguments as code; text piped into one is not data (X3 X4 X8)

git_shared_tree_banned_verbs.purpose: git verbs hard rule 4 bans in the shared checkout, in the guard regex's order

rebase_resume_flags.purpose: git rebase flags that act on a rebase already started, so its start was already checked

rebase_value_flags.purpose: git rebase options whose value is the next word, not an operand

update_ref_value_flags.purpose: git update-ref options whose value is the next word

branch_value_flags.purpose: git branch options whose value is the next word

rtk_rewrite_words.purpose: words rtk rewrite may act on: its --help commands plus raw aliases; a command with none skips the exec

rtk_machine_readable_flags.purpose: flags asking for exact, parseable output: such a command bypasses rtk

rtk_value_subcommands.purpose: git subcommands whose stdout is a value parsed verbatim, so rtk must not wrap them

git_valueless_global_flags.purpose: git global options that take no value; any other option is unknown and fails closed

rtk_go_test_raw_flags.purpose: go test flags whose output rtk's summary drops, named without their dashes

python_import_modules.purpose: stdlib modules a plain edit script imports; none runs a command or loads code

python_runner_options.purpose: managed-environment runners (`uv run`, `poetry run`, ...) and the options that take the next word

patch_write_tools.purpose: patch tools and formatters that rewrite files in place whatever their arguments

formatter_write_flags.purpose: formatter -> flags that make it write files instead of printing

formatter_write_subcommands.purpose: tool -> first argument that makes it write files

print_only_flags.purpose: flags that make a patch tool or formatter print instead of write; * holds every tool's

relay_go_env_flags.purpose: go flags that write files or run other programs; a relay refuses a GOFLAGS carrying one (no dashes)

relay_go_env_vars.purpose: Go variables that can redirect what the toolchain runs or writes; a relay refuses an inline assignment

relay_go_value_flags.purpose: go verb -> value flags a relay's go gate allows, without dashes; the keys are the only gated verbs

relay_go_bool_flags.purpose: go verb -> valueless flags a relay's go gate allows, without dashes

commit_value_flags.purpose: git commit options whose value is the next word; their short letters also end a value cluster

add_stage_all_flags.purpose: git add flags that stage every tracked change when no pathspec is given

removal_operand_commands.purpose: commands that remove every file operand they are given

removal_move_commands.purpose: commands that move their sources away, removing them from where they were

writer_script_flags.purpose: in-place editor -> short flags that take the script as their value; the rest are files to write

writer_operand_commands.purpose: commands that write every file operand they are given

writer_destination_commands.purpose: commands that write their last operand, or the -t directory

read_only_rtk_plain_subcommands.purpose: rtk subcommands that stand for the plain command after them in the read-only check

read_only_plain_commands.purpose: commands the read-only check allows whatever their arguments

read_only_banned_flags.purpose: command or verb -> flags that make an otherwise read-only command write, follow or run

find_exec_flags.purpose: find actions that run a command

find_write_flags.purpose: find actions that delete or write a file

git_read_only_verbs.purpose: git subcommands a read-only run may use, in their plain spelling (drift X6: shell's list differs)

git_read_only_gated_verbs.purpose: read-only git verbs that also write, so only the read forms their argument check names pass

git_read_only_banned_long.purpose: git long flags, abbreviations too, that pick a program, config, repo or output (drift X6)

git_ls_files_flags.purpose: the only git ls-files flags a read-only run may pass

git_worktree_list_flags.purpose: the only flags a read-only git worktree list may pass

git_log_patch_flags.purpose: git log flags that print file contents

claude_code_write_flags.purpose: option names that suggest an output file, a repair or a deletion; any one denies a claude-code verb

claude_code_read_only_verbs.purpose: claude-code group -> verbs a read-only run may call

no_file_commands.purpose: builtins whose arguments are printed, never opened as files

kube_clis.purpose: the kubectl family: a kubectl row of the read-only CLI tables holds for each

kube_credential_kinds.purpose: kubernetes resources whose get or describe output carries a secret or token

read_only_cli_forms.purpose: "tool verb" -> its only flags, none printing env: -x, --x= any, --x=a|b listed, --x=/ owner/repo

read_only_cli_bare_forms.purpose: "tool subcommand" forms of the read-only CLIs that take no flag

read_only_cli_global_flags.purpose: tool -> value flags it may carry before its subcommand

heredoc_data_consumers.purpose: commands that read a heredoc as data; a shell, a writer or a remote run is none

cwd_moving_words.purpose: words that may change the shell's cwd for the segments after them
